Major Wall Street Banks Trim 2026 Oil-Price Forecasts
By Farhan Rafid

Major Wall Street banks have trimmed their oil-price forecasts for this year amid signs that elevated fuel prices are weighing on demand, while expectations for improving oil flows point to softer crude prices ahead.

A survey compiled by The Wall Street Journal, including projections from Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, showed Brent crude is expected to average $78.92 a barrel in the fourth quarter, slightly above the $78.36 projected in July, while West Texas Intermediate is seen at $74.62 a barrel, below the previous projection of $74.97.

The International Energy Agency this month cut its forecast for global oil demand, saying consumption is now expected to decline by 1.6 million barrels a day in 2026, as the continued disruption through the Strait of Hormuz and elevated fuel prices weigh on oil use.

Oil prices jumped Monday after renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran revived concerns over crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude for November delivery rose 3.4% to $91.08 a barrel, while October WTI gained 3.3% to $86.19 a barrel.
According to the Journal's survey, Brent and WTI are forecast to average $83.81 a barrel and $78.79 a barrel, respectively, in 2026, below July projections of $84.52 and $79.73 a barrel.
In the first quarter of 2027, Brent is estimated to average $75.22 a barrel, while WTI is seen at $71.44 a barrel.
